          Celebrating 1,500 WSL Matches: Looking Back on the League's Most Statistically Significant Games
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the 1,500th WSL game set to be played this weekend, we look back at some of the matches that hold statistical significance across the competition’s history.
This weekend will see the 1,500th game in English Women’s Super League history played when Manchester City host Arsenal in one of the most anticipated fixtures of the 2026-27 season.

Ahead of Matchday 5 of the campaign, there have been 1,493 matches played across 17 seasons of WSL action – including the 2017 Spring Series. With six games scheduled before Sunday's showdown at the Etihad Stadium, Manchester City and Arsenal will have the distinction of contesting the league's landmark 1,500th fixture.
To mark the occasion, we look back at some of the most memorable matches in WSL history and the statistics that made them stand out.
The first ever WSL fixture took place on 13 April 2011 with Chelsea hosting Arsenal at Imperial Fields, Mitcham.

Arsenal edged a 1-0 victory thanks to Gilly Flaherty's 35th-minute strike, though chances were at a premium throughout. The two sides combined for just 13 shots and five efforts on target, making it one of the least open contests of the campaign.
The win was one of 10 Arsenal recorded during the inaugural 2011 WSL season, as they went on to finish three points clear of Birmingham City and win the league's first title.
Arsenal are also the team to have secured the biggest margin of victory ever seen in WSL history (+10), as they thrashed Bristol City 11-1 at Meadow Park in December 2019 under Joe Montemurro.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, this is also the highest-scoring WSL fixture of all time (12).

The warning signs were there for Bristol City. Rooted to the foot of the table without a single win to their name, they travelled to face the reigning champions knowing they were up against one of the most dominant sides in the league.
What followed was a mismatch of historic proportions.

Ten of Arsenal’s goals were either scored (6) or assisted (4) by Vivianne Miedema, who set WSL records for the most goals, assists and goal involvements by a player in a single WSL match. Those records still stand, although Chelsea’s Guro Reiten equalled the Dutch forward’s single-game assist record with four against Leicester City on 3 December 2022.

Two WSL matches have featured as many as nine different goalscorers, excluding own goals: Chelsea's 9-0 victory over Bristol City in September 2020 and Brighton & Hove Albion's thrilling 7-3 win against the Robins in March 2024.

Chelsea’s first home game of 2020-21 was a treat for their fans at Kingsmeadow. The Blues ran riot, scoring nine times from as many different players. Millie Bright, Sam Kerr, Niamh Charles, Maren Mjelde, Fran Kirby, Melanie Leupolz, Erin Cuthbert, Pernille Harder and Bethany England all found the net in a historic display.

Three and a half years later, Brighton's 7-3 victory at Ashton Gate produced another game with nine different goalscorers. Of the 10 goals scored, only Elisabeth Terland (two) found the net more than once.

Katie Robinson, Madison Haley, Pauline Bremer, Tatiana Pinto and Vicky Losada were Brighton's other scorers, while Amalie Thestrup, Brooke Aspin and Megan Connolly found the net for Bristol City in defeat, making it one of the most entertaining and free-scoring matches in WSL history.
One other WSL record was set in a match between Chelsea and Bristol City, too.

Chelsea's 6-0 win over Manchester City in February 2019 remains the only WSL match to feature two hat-trick scorers. Bethany England and Fran Kirby shared the six goals between them, taking turns to find the net throughout the contest. Kirby scored Chelsea's first, third and fifth goals, while England struck the others.
Kirby scored another hat-trick in their next game, a 4-0 win over Liverpool, meaning two of her three hat-tricks in the competition came in back-to-back appearances.
Only Vivianne Miedema (five) and Khadija Shaw (eight) have recorded more WSL hat-tricks than Kirby and England, who remain tied on three apiece.
